description: Test cases for doc-guardrail-generation: producing a single-pass guardrail Markdown file by instantiating assets/guardrail.template.md, with every rule classified by how it is verified (deterministic vs semantic) and carrying a project-unique, domain-prefixed id (<PREFIX>-NN) that is never renumbered or reused.

cases.name: full-arguments-produce-complete-guardrail
cases.description: Name, output folder, candidate rules and a source of truth are all given. The output instantiates the template end to end: scope line, the verbatim on-breach paragraph, both rule layers, runnable commands and a source-of-truth section. No template comment or placeholder survives.

input.prompt: Create a guardrail named docker-compose-services in guardrails/. It governs our Docker Compose service definitions: every service pins an image digest, no container runs as root, secrets are never plain environment values, and every service declares a healthcheck. Source of truth: skills/code-backend-nestjs/SKILL.md and the Compose Specification at https://compose-spec.io.

cases.name: topic-only-derives-name-and-default-path
cases.description: Only the topic is given — no name and no output folder. The skill derives a kebab-case file name from the domain, appends the -checklist suffix, and writes into the repository's existing guardrails/ directory without asking for either.

input.prompt: I need a guardrail for our GitHub Actions workflows: actions pinned to a full commit SHA, no plaintext secrets in the YAML, and an explicit permissions block on every job.

cases.name: no-domain-asks-before-writing
cases.description: A request that names neither a guardrail nor a subject to regulate must stop and ask what the guardrail governs. Nothing is written to disk.

cases.name: existing-guardrail-not-overwritten-silently
cases.description: When the target file already exists, the skill reports the path and offers regenerate / skip / compare instead of overwriting it.

input.prompt: Create a guardrail for E2E testing with Cypress and Cucumber in guardrails/.

cases.name: unverifiable-rules-land-in-the-semantic-layer
cases.description: The core classification behaviour. Rules a named command can decide go to the deterministic layer with tool and severity; rules requiring judgement go to the semantic layer as prose that carries its guardrail id but no (error)/(warn) marker.

input.prompt: Create a guardrail named api-error-handling in guardrails/. Rules: every endpoint returns application/problem+json (we run Spectral), no stack trace is ever serialised into a response body (greppable), and error messages must be meaningful to the end user and must never leak internal domain terminology.

cases.name: missing-source-of-truth-warns-and-does-not-invent
cases.description: A cited source-of-truth file that does not exist must be reported, not silently ignored and not fabricated. The skill asks whether to continue from the request alone rather than inventing rules attributed to the missing file.

input.prompt: Create a guardrail for our Terraform modules based on docs/standards/terraform-standard.md

cases.name: dry-run-plans-without-writing
cases.description: With --dry-run the skill reports the target path and the rules it would classify into each layer, and writes nothing to disk.

input.prompt: Create a guardrail for our REST API versioning conventions --dry-run

cases.name: adapts-to-modified-template-without-skill-edits
cases.description: Guards the decoupling: the output shape comes from the template at run time, never from SKILL.md. A template carrying an extra section and a renamed placeholder must flow through to the output with no edit to SKILL.md.

input.prompt: Create a guardrail for our database migrations, using the template at .tmp/guardrail.template.modified.md
template_mutations: insert section '## Rollback expectations' with placeholder '[How the change is reverted and who signs it off]'
rename placeholder '[concrete scope]' to '[the exact scope this guardrail binds]'

not_contains: [How the change is reverted and who signs it off]

cases.name: checklist-suffix-is-idempotent
cases.description: The output file always carries the -checklist suffix exactly once. A name the user already wrote with the suffix is used as it is, never suffixed twice.

input.prompt: Create a guardrail named release-notes-checklist in guardrails/. Rules: every entry links the commit that introduced it (greppable), the version heading follows semver, and the wording of each entry is meaningful to a user of the product rather than to its authors.

cases.name: every-rule-carries-a-domain-prefixed-id
cases.description: Every rule in both layers carries one id of the form <PREFIX>-NN: the prefix the user gave, two fixed digits, bold, first token after the checkbox, one sequence continuing from the deterministic layer into the semantic one. Flat families (G-01) and mixed padding (DCS-1, DCS-001) never appear. The Rule IDs line under the scope names the prefix.

input.prompt: Create a guardrail named docker-compose-services in guardrails/, use the prefix DCS. Rules: every service pins an image digest (greppable), no container runs as root (greppable), every service declares a healthcheck (greppable), and the healthcheck actually exercises the service's real readiness rather than a trivial command.

cases.name: update-appends-ids-and-never-renumbers
cases.description: Under --update the existing rules keep their ids untouched and a new rule takes the next free number at the end of its layer. Nothing is renumbered, no gap is closed, and the prefix does not change.

input.prompt: Add a rule to guardrails/code-security-checklist.md --update: no documented command disables the package manager's signature or checksum verification (greppable).
input.existing_file_facts: The existing file uses the prefix SEC with ids SEC-01 to SEC-24 and no retired ids.

cases.name: prefix-collision-is-refused
cases.description: A prefix already used by a sibling guardrail in the output folder is never reused. When the derived prefix collides, the skill says so, proposes a distinct one and either asks or proceeds with the distinct prefix; it never writes a second file whose ids repeat the sibling's.

input.prompt: Create a guardrail for secrets management in our deployment manifests in guardrails/: no secret value is inlined in a manifest (greppable), every secret is referenced by name from the vault (greppable), and secret names describe what the secret unlocks rather than where it is used.
input.existing_file_facts: The sibling guardrails/code-security-checklist.md already uses the prefix SEC.
